messages:
danielle: quick heads-up — saw a spike of OOMs on the streaming infra during long multi-turn chats. root cause looks like KV prefill + fragmented workspace allocations. happened on dedicated nodes under burst load.

marco: ugh. is this the prefill path that allocates separate buffers per-request before decode starts?

danielle: yes — we prefill the full KV for the prefix at request arrival. when many concurrent long streams arrive we end up with many small allocations and high external fragmentation. allocator stats (one sample):
```
GPU total 40GB, used 31.8GB, free chunks: 420, avg_chunk: 72KB, largest_free: 6.2GB
workspace_reserved: 6.0GB, workspace_active: 4.7GB
frag_metric: 0.42  # (1 - sum_free/total_free_est)
per-request-kv-avg: 9.4MB, concurrent_prefills: 220
OOMs: 18 in 10m during burst
```

ryan: can you paste the reproducer? i want to run with slab reuse flags.

danielle: repro (short):
```
# run locally on a small cluster
./run_loadtest --model redwood-7b-q4 --concurrency 200 --streaming --prompt-file long_prompts.txt \n  --prefill-mode=full --prefill-cap=unbounded --seed=42
```
I also attached a heap trace in /tmp/kv-oom-176864.log (linked in thread).

priya: two quick ideas: 1) enforce a per-request prefill cap (max_prefill_entries or max_prefill_bytes) so new requests don't hog tiny free chunks; 2) prefer decode-driven prefill where we only materialize KV entries as decode needs them (lazy prefill). Both reduce peak allocation.

marco: agree on cap. also suggest a hybrid eviction: keep a small LRU for recently-decoded entries, and allow eviction of prefill-only entries first. that reduces user-visible regressions.

ryan: trying slab reuse + smaller workspace per-stream now. change tested locally:
```json
{
  "allocator": {
    "reuse_slabs": true,
    "prefer_slab_size": 2097152,
    "workspace_reserve_bytes": 2147483648,
    "workspace_per_stream_max": 524288
  },
  "kv": {
    "prefill_cap_bytes": 15728640,   // 15MB per-request
    "eviction_policy": "prefill-first-lru",
    "fragmentation_monitor_ms": 10000
  }
}
```
results: fragmentation dropped from ~0.42 -> ~0.18, OOMs -> 2 in same load window.

sasha: nice. couple of metrics to add to dashboard: concurrent_prefills, avg_prefill_bytes/request, frag_metric, slab_reuse_hit_rate. we should correlate with tail latency (p95/p99).

marco: also note decode path changes: if we switch to lazy prefill, we must ensure the kernel selection logic can handle missing KV quickly (fallback kernels vs blocking prefill). otherwise we trade OOMs for higher p99.

priya: good point — recommend canary: enable per-request prefill cap + slab reuse on a fraction of nodes, route 10% of traffic with long prompts. monitor p95/p99 and OOM rate for 30m. if p99 increases > 15% revert.

danielle: agreed. i'll open a canary run and collect perf counters. attaching initial profiling snippet showing kernel-switch overhead for lazy prefill vs full prefill:
```
- full-prefill: avg_kernels_per_token=1.05, extra_wait_ms=2.1, p99_token_time=12.8ms
- lazy-prefill: avg_kernels_per_token=1.18, extra_wait_ms=6.7, p99_token_time=17.9ms
```

marco: sounds acceptable if OOMs go way down. prefer incremental: 1) per-request cap, 2) slab reuse, 3) hybrid eviction, 4) evaluate lazy prefill if still needed.

ryan: launching canary with flags from my local test. will push config to staging group "kv-frag-canary" and add 10 nodes. command: `./deployer canary apply --group kv-frag-canary --config configs/kv-prefill-tune.json`

perf-bot: [alert] canary started by ryan at 1768641625. monitoring p95/p99, oom_count, frag_metric.

danielle: action items:
- danielle: collect detailed allocator histograms + heaptrace if OOM (next 2h)
- ryan: deploy canary + enable slab reuse (in progress)
- sasha: add dashboard panels and alerts for frag_metric & concurrent_prefills
- marco: draft eviction policy PR (prefer prefill-only evict first)

priya: ping me when canary hits 30m, i'll validate SLA impacts and rollback criteria.

marco: thanks — small follow-up ask: add a unit test for allocator that simulates many small prefill allocations to catch regressions.

danielle: noted. will follow up with logs and initial run results. :+1:
